question: Which of the following vitamins helps to keep our skin and eyes healthy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin A (Retinol) is essential for healthy skin and good eyesight. It forms rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment of the retina, and maintains the health of epithelial (skin and mucous-membrane) tissue. (विटामिन A — त्वचा और आँखों के लिए)

• Its deficiency causes night blindness (nyctalopia), xerophthalmia (dryness of the eye) and rough, dry skin.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sources of Vitamin A: carrots, green leafy vegetables, papaya, mango, milk, butter, egg yolk, cod-liver oil. Plant sources supply beta-carotene, which the body converts into Vitamin A.

• Vitamin D (Calciferol) — bones and teeth; deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia.

• Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) — immunity and gums; deficiency causes scurvy.

• Vitamin B complex — deficiency of B1 causes beriberi, of B3 pellagra, of B12 pernicious anaemia.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C.

• Vitamin A is also called the "anti-infective vitamin" because it protects the linings of the respiratory and digestive tracts.

question: According to the 2011 census, what is the literacy rate of New Delhi District?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 88.01 percent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of 2011, the literacy rate of the New Delhi district was 88.01 percent. (नई दिल्ली ज़िले की साक्षरता दर — 88.01 प्रतिशत)

• Literacy in the Census is measured for the population aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census of India and the 7th after Independence. Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

• India's overall literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate among states (94%) and Bihar the lowest (61.8%); Lakshadweep was the highest among UTs.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act, 1948, by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The first complete census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: India accounts for what percent of total geographical area of the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.4 percent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India occupies about 2.4 percent of the world's total geographical (land) area, while supporting roughly 17–18 percent of the world's population. (विश्व के भू-क्षेत्र का लगभग 2.4 प्रतिशत)

• India's total area is 3.287 million sq km, making it the 7th largest country in the world by area.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The seven largest countries by area: Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil, Australia, India.

• India's mainland extends from 8°4' N to 37°6' N latitude and 68°7' E to 97°25' E longitude.

• India's land frontier is about 15,200 km and its total coastline (including islands) is about 7,516.6 km.

NOTE

• The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) divides India almost into two halves, passing through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

question: Which Guru of Kuchipudi dance form received Padma Bhushan in the year 1998?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam (1929–2012), the legendary maestro of the Kuchipudi dance form of Andhra Pradesh, was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1998. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी)

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai (1963) and choreographed many celebrated dance-dramas, taking Kuchipudi from village performance to the international stage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Uday Shankar was a pioneer of modern/creative dance in India.

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was the greatest exponent of Odissi (Odisha).

• Guru Bipin Singh was the doyen of Manipuri dance.

NOTE

• Kuchipudi originates from the village of Kuchelapuram in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh. It combines nritta, nritya and natya, and its famous items include the Tarangam (dancing on the rim of a brass plate) and Bhama Kalapam.

• The eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: The Jain temple at Pattadakal was built by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtrakutas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jain temple (Jaina Narayana temple) at Pattadakal, in the Bagalkot district of Karnataka, was built by the Rashtrakutas in the 9th century CE, most likely during the reign of Amoghavarsha I or Krishna II. (पट्टडकल का जैन मंदिर — राष्ट्रकूट)

• The rest of the Pattadakal group of monuments was built mainly by the Chalukyas of Badami, which is why this Jain temple stands apart from the main cluster.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Pattadakal was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987. It is famous for the blend of Nagara (North Indian) and Dravida (South Indian) temple styles.

• The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Queen Lokamahadevi to commemorate her husband Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas of Kanchipuram.

• Nearby heritage sites: Badami (cave temples) and Aihole (called the "cradle of Indian temple architecture").

NOTE

• The Rashtrakutas (8th–10th century CE) ruled from Manyakheta and are best known for the magnificent rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora, built by Krishna I.

question: Which among the following states has the highest sex ratio in India according to the Census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, Kerala had the highest sex ratio among Indian states — 1084 females per 1000 males. (केरल — सर्वाधिक लिंगानुपात)

• Sex ratio is defined in India as the number of females per 1000 males.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's overall sex ratio in 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males (up from 933 in 2001).

• Haryana had the lowest sex ratio among states (879); among Union Territories, Puducherry was highest (1037) and Daman & Diu lowest (618).

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, the lowest since Independence — a matter of serious concern.

NOTE

• Kerala also leads India in literacy (94%), life expectancy and the Human Development Index, largely due to its investments in education and public health.

• The scheme "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao" (launched 2015 from Panipat, Haryana) targets the declining child sex ratio.

question: Which among the following elements is used in moisturising creams and soaps because of its hygroscopic properties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glycerol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Glycerol (glycerine, propane-1,2,3-triol) is strongly hygroscopic — it absorbs and retains moisture from the air. This is why it is added to moisturising creams, lotions, soaps and cosmetics to keep the skin soft and hydrated. (ग्लिसरॉल — नमी सोखने वाला)

• It is a colourless, odourless, sweet-tasting, viscous liquid and is a by-product of soap manufacture (saponification) of fats and oils.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Galena is the chief ore of lead (PbS) — lead sulphide.

• Ethanol (C2H5OH) is an alcohol used in beverages, sanitisers and as a fuel additive; it is drying rather than moisturising.

• Freon is the trade name for chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) once used as refrigerants; they damage the ozone layer and were phased out under the Montreal Protocol (1987).

NOTE

• Glycerol is also used to make nitroglycerine (an explosive and a heart medicine), in food as a sweetener/humectant, and in pharmaceutical syrups.

• A hygroscopic substance absorbs moisture from air; other examples are silica gel, calcium chloride and concentrated sulphuric acid.

question: Which UK Prime Minister resigned on 20th October, 2022 after serving for 44 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liz Truss.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Liz Truss announced her resignation as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on 20 October 2022, after just 44 days in office — the shortest tenure of any British Prime Minister in history. (लिज़ ट्रस — मात्र 44 दिन)

• Her resignation followed the market turmoil triggered by her government's "mini-budget" of large unfunded tax cuts, which caused the pound to fall sharply.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She had taken office on 6 September 2022, succeeding Boris Johnson, who resigned amid a series of political scandals.

• She was succeeded by Rishi Sunak, who became the first British Prime Minister of Indian origin on 25 October 2022.

• Theresa May was UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019 (the second woman to hold the post after Margaret Thatcher).

NOTE

• The UK is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy. Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022 — just two days after appointing Liz Truss — and was succeeded by King Charles III.

question: Who among the following has been awarded with Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021 for “Para Shooting”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Avani Lekhara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Avani Lekhara received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021 for Para Shooting. (अवनि लेखरा — पैरा निशानेबाज़ी)

• At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics (held in 2021) she won a gold medal in the 10 m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event and a bronze in the 50 m Rifle 3 Positions SH1, becoming the first Indian woman to win a Paralympic gold.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Krishna Nagar won gold in para badminton (SH6) and Pramod Bhagat gold in para badminton (SL3) at Tokyo.

• Sumit Antil won gold in the men's javelin throw F64 with a world record.

• All of them were also honoured in the same year's national sports awards.

NOTE

• The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in August 2021. It is India's highest sporting honour.

• Major Dhyan Chand — "The Wizard" of hockey — won Olympic golds in 1928, 1932 and 1936; his birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day.

question: The prehistoric period in the early development of human beings is commonly known as the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Old stone age.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Old Stone Age (Palaeolithic Age) is the earliest prehistoric period in the development of human beings. It covers roughly 2 million BCE to 10,000 BCE. (पुरापाषाण काल)

• In this age humans were hunter-gatherers, used rough, unpolished stone tools (hand-axes, cleavers, choppers), lived in caves and rock shelters, and did not know agriculture, pottery or metals. The discovery of fire belongs to this age.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age, c. 10,000–6000 BCE) — use of tiny tools called microliths; beginning of animal domestication; famous site Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) with rock paintings.

• Neolithic / New Stone Age (c. 6000–1000 BCE) — polished stone tools, beginning of agriculture, pottery and settled village life; sites like Mehrgarh, Burzahom and Chirand.

• Iron Age comes much later, after the Chalcolithic (copper-stone) and Bronze ages.

NOTE

• The Indian Palaeolithic is divided into Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. Important sites: Soan valley, Bhimbetka, Hunsgi, Attirampakkam and Belan valley.

question: Which among the following is NOT a Jovian planet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mercury.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jovian planets (also called gas giants or outer planets) are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. They are large, gaseous, low in density and have many moons and ring systems.

• Mercury is not a Jovian planet — it is a terrestrial (rocky/inner) planet, along with Venus, Earth and Mars. (बुध — स्थलीय ग्रह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun; it has the shortest year (88 Earth days) and no natural satellite.

• Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System; Saturn is famous for its bright rings and is the least dense planet (it would float on water).

• Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun and is called the windiest planet.

NOTE

• "Jovian" comes from Jove, another name for the Roman god Jupiter.

• Terrestrial planets are separated from the Jovian planets by the asteroid belt lying between Mars and Jupiter.

question: Article 17 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abolition of Untouchability.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 17 of the Indian Constitution abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form. The enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability is a punishable offence. (अनुच्छेद 17 — अस्पृश्यता का अंत)

• It is one of the few Fundamental Rights available against private individuals as well as the State, and it is absolute — no exceptions are permitted.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 14 — Equality before law and equal protection of the laws.

• Article 15 — Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

• Article 16 — Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

• Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

• Article 21A — Right to Education (added by the 86th Amendment, 2002, for children aged 6–14).

NOTE

• Articles 14–18 together constitute the Right to Equality.

• Parliament enacted the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, and later the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 to enforce Article 17.

question: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, famous Indian scientist's, autobiography is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wings of Fire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wings of Fire: An Autobiography" is the autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, co-written with Arun Tiwari and published in 1999. (विंग्स ऑफ फायर — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम की आत्मकथा)

• It traces his journey from a humble childhood in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, to becoming the architect of India's missile programme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dr. Kalam was the 11th President of India (2002–2007), popularly called the "Missile Man of India" and the "People's President". He received the Bharat Ratna in 1997.

• His other books: India 2020, Ignited Minds, My Journey, Turning Points, Transcendence.

• One Life is Not Enough — autobiography of K. Natwar Singh; Waiting for a Visa — autobiographical notes of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar; The Race of My Life — autobiography of Milkha Singh.

NOTE

• Dr. Kalam worked at ISRO and DRDO; he was the project director of India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle SLV-III, which put Rohini into orbit in 1980, and played a key role in the Pokhran-II nuclear tests of 1998.

• His birthday, 15 October, is observed as World Students' Day.

question: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma, an Indian musician and composer was the foremost exponent of the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santoor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma (1938–2022) was the foremost exponent of the Santoor, a hundred-stringed trapezoid instrument of Jammu and Kashmir. (पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा — संतूर)

• He is credited with transforming the santoor from a folk instrument of Kashmiri Sufiana music into a full-fledged Indian classical concert instrument.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1991) and the Padma Vibhushan (2001).

• Along with flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, he composed music for films such as Silsila, Chandni, Lamhe and Darr under the joint name "Shiv–Hari".

• The santoor is played with a pair of light wooden mallets called "kalam".

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tata Vadya (stringed — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushira Vadya (wind — flute, shehnai), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam) and Ghana Vadya (solid/struck — manjira, jaltarang). The santoor is a struck stringed instrument.

question: Which among the following sessions of Indian National Congress was the first session to be presided by a lady?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta - 1917.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1917 was presided over by Dr. Annie Besant, who thus became the first woman President of the INC. (कलकत्ता अधिवेशन 1917 — एनी बेसेंट)

• She was an Irish-born theosophist and social reformer who founded the Home Rule League (1916) and the newspaper New India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kanpur session, 1925 — presided over by Sarojini Naidu, the first Indian woman President of the INC (the "Nightingale of India").

• Lahore session, 1929 — presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru; it adopted the resolution of "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence), and 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

• Surat session, 1907 — the famous Surat Split between the Moderates and the Extremists; presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh.

NOTE

• The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume; its first session (Bombay, 1885) was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

• Nellie Sengupta presided over the Calcutta session of 1933 — the third woman to head the Congress.

question: The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 aimed at unifying the ______ Municipal Corporations of Delhi to ensure a robust setup for synergised and strategic planning and optimal utilisation of resources.
solution_text:
The correct answer is three.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2022 merged the three municipal corporations of Delhi — the North Delhi Municipal Corporation, South Delhi Municipal Corporation and East Delhi Municipal Corporation — back into a single unified Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). (तीन निगमों का एकीकरण)

• The stated aim was synergised and strategic planning, optimal utilisation of resources and a financially stronger civic body.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Municipal Corporation of Delhi was originally created under the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, and was trifurcated in 2012.

• The Bill was passed by Parliament in April 2022 and came into force from 22 May 2022. It also reduced the number of wards to not more than 250.

NOTE

• Urban local bodies were given constitutional status by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) to the Constitution.

• Types of urban local bodies: Municipal Corporation (large cities), Municipality/Municipal Council (smaller cities) and Nagar Panchayat (transitional areas).

question: The Walker Cup is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Walker Cup is a golf trophy. It is contested every two years between teams of amateur golfers from the United States and a combined team from Great Britain and Ireland. (वॉकर कप — गोल्फ)

• It is named after George Herbert Walker, a former president of the United States Golf Association, and was first played in 1922.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other golf trophies: Ryder Cup (USA vs Europe, professionals), Solheim Cup (women professionals), Presidents Cup, and the four majors — The Masters, US Open, The Open Championship and PGA Championship.

• Hockey trophies: Agha Khan Cup, Beighton Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy, Rangaswami Cup.

• Chess: Linares Trophy, Khel Ratna is national; Football: FIFA World Cup, Durand Cup, Santosh Trophy.

NOTE

• Golf terms: birdie (one under par), eagle (two under par), bogey (one over par), par, albatross, hole-in-one, caddie, tee, putt.

• India's leading golfers include Jeev Milkha Singh, Anirban Lahiri and Aditi Ashok.

question: Galvanisation is a process in which a protective ______ coating is applied on iron to prevent it from rusting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is zinc.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Galvanisation is the process of applying a protective coating of zinc on iron or steel to prevent rusting (corrosion). (जस्ता / ज़िंक की परत चढ़ाना)

• Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes in preference to the iron beneath — this is called sacrificial protection. Even if the coating is scratched, the exposed iron remains protected.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rust is hydrated ferric oxide (Fe2O3·xH2O); rusting requires both oxygen (air) and moisture (water).

• Other methods of preventing corrosion: painting, greasing/oiling, electroplating, anodising, alloying (e.g., stainless steel).

• Electroplating with chromium, nickel or silver is done mainly for shine and wear resistance, not sacrificial protection.

NOTE

• Zinc (Zn) — atomic number 30. Galvanised iron sheets (GI sheets) are widely used for roofing, buckets, pipes and fencing.

• Stainless steel is an alloy of iron, chromium (about 18%) and nickel (about 8%) and does not rust.

question: Which among the following is the famous harvest festival of Meghalaya, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nongkrem festival.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ka Pomblang Nongkrem" (Nongkrem Dance festival) is the famous harvest/thanksgiving festival of the Khasi tribe of Meghalaya. It is held annually at Smit, near Shillong. (नोंगक्रेम — मेघालय)

• It is a five-day religious festival in which the Khasis thank the deity Ka Blei Synshar for a good harvest and pray for peace and prosperity; a goat sacrifice (Pomblang) is a central ritual.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chapchar Kut is the spring festival of Mizoram, celebrated after the completion of jhum (slash-and-burn) clearing.

• Hornbill festival is the "Festival of Festivals" of Nagaland, held at Kisama every December.

• Sunburn is a commercial electronic dance music festival held in Goa/Pune, not a tribal harvest festival.

NOTE

• Other festivals of Meghalaya: Wangala (the hundred-drums harvest festival of the Garo tribe), Behdienkhlam (of the Jaintia tribe) and Shad Suk Mynsiem (the spring dance of the Khasis).

• Meghalaya, "the abode of clouds", was carved out of Assam in 1972; its capital is Shillong.

question: Bharatanatyam dance is associated with which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, one of the oldest classical dances of India. (भरतनाट्यम — तमिलनाडु)

• It grew out of the Sadir/Dasiattam performed by devadasis in the temples of Tamil Nadu and is based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Its repertoire follows a fixed order: Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana and Shlokam.

• Famous exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale (who founded Kalakshetra), Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam and Vyjayanthimala.

• The name is often explained as BHAva (expression) + RAga (melody) + TAla (rhythm) + Natyam (dance).

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu; Kathak – Uttar Pradesh; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Odissi – Odisha; Manipuri – Manipur; Sattriya – Assam.

• Folk dances: Lavani – Maharashtra; Garba – Gujarat; Bhangra – Punjab; Bihu – Assam.

question: Indian Railways plan to become Net Zero Carbon Emitter by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2030.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indian Railways has set the target of becoming a "Net Zero Carbon Emitter" by 2030, which would make it the world's first railway system to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. (2030 तक नेट ज़ीरो कार्बन उत्सर्जक)

• The plan rests on 100% electrification of broad-gauge routes, large-scale use of solar and wind energy, energy-efficient locomotives, head-on generation in coaches and extensive afforestation along tracks.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Indian Railways is the fourth largest railway network in the world (after the USA, China and Russia) and one of the world's largest employers.

• The first passenger train in India ran from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane on 16 April 1853, a distance of about 34 km.

• India as a nation has announced a net-zero target of 2070 (declared by the Prime Minister at COP26, Glasgow, 2021, as part of the "Panchamrit" commitments).

NOTE

• "Net zero" means balancing the greenhouse gases emitted with an equivalent amount removed or offset, so that the net addition to the atmosphere is zero.

question: What does ‘F’ stand for in FRBM Act, 2003 of Indian economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• FRBM stands for the "Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management" Act, so the letter "F" stands for "Fiscal". (राजकोषीय उत्तरदायित्व एवं बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम)

• The Act was passed in 2003 and came into force in July 2004. Its objective is to bring fiscal discipline, reduce the fiscal deficit and public debt, and ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FRBM Act required the government to reduce the fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP and eliminate the revenue deficit.

• It mandates the presentation of statements along with the Budget: the Medium Term Fiscal Policy Statement, the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement and the Macro-Economic Framework Statement.

• The N. K. Singh Committee (2017) reviewed the Act and recommended a debt-to-GDP ratio of 60% (40% Centre + 20% States) as the medium-term anchor.

NOTE

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure – Total receipts (excluding borrowings).

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure – Revenue receipts.

• Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments.

question: Who among the following introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital - the two basic coins of the Sultanate period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iltutmish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shamsuddin Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, which became the two basic coins of the Delhi Sultanate. (इल्तुतमिश — चाँदी का टंका और ताँबे का जीतल)

• The silver tanka weighed about 175 grains and was the ancestor of the modern rupee; the jital was the small change used in everyday transactions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Iltutmish belonged to the Slave (Mamluk/Ilbari) dynasty and is regarded as the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate. He shifted the capital from Lahore to Delhi, created the Iqta system and the nobility group known as the "Chahalgani/Turkan-i-Chihalgani" (Corps of Forty).

• He completed the Qutub Minar begun by Qutubuddin Aibak, and obtained a letter of investiture (mansur) from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229, giving legal status to his rule.

• Alauddin Khilji is famous for market/price control regulations; Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency; Ibrahim Lodi was defeated at Panipat (1526) by Babur.

NOTE

• Dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in order: Slave (1206–90), Khilji (1290–1320), Tughlaq (1320–1414), Sayyid (1414–51) and Lodi (1451–1526).

question: Which of the following states is the leading producer of cotton in India, as of November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gujarat is the leading producer of cotton in India (as of November 2022), followed by Maharashtra and Telangana. (गुजरात — कपास का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक)

• The black soil (regur/black cotton soil) of the Deccan Trap region, which retains moisture well, together with a warm climate and moderate rainfall, makes Gujarat ideal for cotton cultivation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Cotton is a kharif crop, sown around June–July and harvested from October onwards; it needs 21–30°C temperature, 50–100 cm rainfall and about 210 frost-free days.

• India is among the largest producers of cotton in the world along with China and the USA.

• Cotton is called "white gold" and is the mainstay of India's textile industry.

NOTE

• Leading producers of other crops: Rice – West Bengal; Wheat – Uttar Pradesh; Sugarcane – Uttar Pradesh; Jute – West Bengal; Tea – Assam; Coffee – Karnataka; Groundnut – Gujarat; Pulses – Madhya Pradesh.

question: Who was the President of Swaraj Party formed in the year 1922?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittaranjan Das.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swaraj Party was formed on 1 January 1923 (following the Gaya session of the Congress in December 1922) with Chittaranjan Das (Deshbandhu) as its President and Motilal Nehru as its Secretary. (चित्तरंजन दास — अध्यक्ष, स्वराज पार्टी)

• It arose after the sudden withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement (February 1922) following the Chauri Chaura incident.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Swarajists (called "Pro-changers") wanted to enter the legislative councils and obstruct the government from within; the "No-changers" (Rajendra Prasad, Sardar Patel, C. Rajagopalachari) opposed council entry and favoured constructive village work.

• The party did well in the 1923 elections to the Central Legislative Assembly and provincial councils, and blocked several government proposals.

• C. R. Das was known as "Deshbandhu"; he defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case and the Chittagong/Barisal accused, and died in 1925.

NOTE

• The Swaraj Party functioned as a group within the Congress, not as a separate rival organisation. After C. R. Das's death in 1925 the party gradually weakened.
